dedupe_keys.name: global data alliance cross border data policy index

description: The Cross-Border Data Policy Index, published by the Global Data Alliance in July 2023, rates nearly 100 economies on how open or restrictive their rules are for moving data across borders. It is built on legal analysis of national laws, regulations and measures that restrict data transfers or require data to be stored locally, covering privacy and data protection, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, law enforcement access and trade commitments, and gives both a quantitative score and a qualitative assessment. Economies are grouped into four levels: 45 relatively open, 33 restrictive, 6 highly restrictive and 2 extremely restrictive. The Alliance also published a global inventory of domestic rules on data localisation drawn from privacy laws. Related work by others, such as the ITIF data restrictiveness index built from OECD product market regulation indicators, reports that nearly 100 data localisation measures were in force in 40 countries by early 2023. Coverage: about 100 economies, one edition. Format and access: PDF report and methodology, free. Caveats: produced by an industry coalition that favours open data flows; a single snapshot; national rules change quickly. Simulation uses: constraints on where data and cloud workloads can be moved in failover and relocation scenarios, and context for siting of data centres driven by localisation rules. Related records: TeleGeography international bandwidth data show the physical flows these rules govern.
